# Contract

`admin.obj.core.contract` · v2.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> A binding commitment between us and a counterparty, held as an obligation set with a clock on it rather than as a file in a folder. Three facts about a contract are load-bearing and none of them are on the front page: what it obliges US to do and by when, how much notice we must give to leave, and whether it renews itself if we say nothing. Everything the administrative function does with a contract after signature — diarising, briefing, benchmarking, exiting — is scheduled backwards from expiry minus the notice period. By the time the expiry date appears in anyone's diary the decision has already been taken, by default, in favour of the counterparty.


**The discriminator.** The executed document is EVIDENCE of the contract; the contract is the obligation set and the exit window. If what you are holding cannot tell you the last day we may walk away and what we owe before then, you are holding a Document, not a Contract.


Also called: `Agreement`, `MSA`, `Master Services Agreement`, `Order Form`, `Statement of Work`, `Terms of Engagement`, `Call-off`


### Questions this object answers

- What is the last date on which we can still decide not to renew this, and who has to decide by then?
- What does this contract oblige US to do, when is the next one due, and is any of it already late?
- If we say nothing, what happens — and what does the silence cost, in money and in months?
- Could we enforce this today? Can we produce a fully executed counterpart within a day?
- Is this spend under paper at all, or is the invoice the only agreement we have?
- Who may sign this value, and did the person who signed it hold that authority?
- Has the price risen since signature, and did anybody approve the rise or merely pay it?


### What it is NOT responsible for

- NOT the executed PDF. admin.obj.core.document owns version, classification, retention and where the file lives.
- NOT the counterparty. admin.obj.core.vendor owns diligence state, bank details, concentration and substitutability.
- NOT the money. admin.obj.core.invoice owns what was billed; admin.obj.core.budget_line owns whether we could afford to commit it.
- NOT the statutory duties that exist whether or not anyone signed anything — admin.obj.core.compliance_obligation owns those. A contract creates obligations; it does not create law.
- NOT the service targets and credits — admin.obj.core.service_level owns those, and the credits nobody claims.
- NOT the authority to sign. admin.obj.core.approval owns the route and the threshold; this object owns only whether the route was followed.

## Preconditions

- **`ct.counterparty_resolved`** The other side is resolved to a vendor record, not to a name in an email signature. _(unmet → Degrade, do not block. Create the contract object against an unresolved counterparty and raise vendor onboarding as the dependency — refusing to record the contract until procurement catches up is how contracts get negotiated entirely outside the register.
)_
- **`ct.term_has_been_read`** end_at and notice_period_days come from the instrument, not from an assumption or last year's register row. _(unmet → Block any statement about the renewal window and say why. An invented notice deadline is worse than none: it produces a confident diary entry on the wrong date and stops anyone looking again.
)_
- **`ct.auto_renew_default_applied`** Where the auto-renewal clause has not been read, the contract is treated as auto-renewing. _(unmet → Degrade to the pessimistic default and flag it as an assumption rather than a fact. The asymmetry runs one way — a needless diary entry costs an hour, a missed window costs a renewal term.
)_
- **`ct.named_owner_exists`** A named human owns the renewal decision — not a function, not a mailbox. _(unmet → Route to the head of the consuming function to name one. Do not route to procurement: procurement will renew it on the strength of the fact that it was renewed last year.
)_
- **`ct.executed_counterpart_locatable`** A fully executed counterpart can be produced, or its absence is recorded as a known gap. _(unmet → Degrade. Continue to administer the contract but mark enforceability_gap true, so the gap surfaces in a renewal negotiation rather than in a dispute.
)_
- **`ct.budget_line_identified`** Committed spend has a budget line to consume, resolved before signature rather than at the first invoice. _(unmet → Block execution above the policy threshold. Commitment accounting only works if the commitment is recorded at commitment.)_
- **`ct.dpa_precedes_data_flow`** Where personal data will flow, an executed DPA and an Article 30 entry exist before the first transfer. _(unmet → Block the data flow, not the contract. The two are separable, and treating them as one is why the DPA is signed six months late.)_


## Constraints

- **`ct.exit_only_within_window`** Where termination_for_convenience is false, the only exit is notice served before notice_deadline_at.
- **`ct.service_method_binds`** Notice must be served by notice_method to notice_recipient. No other method constitutes service, however reasonable it looks.
- **`ct.signature_authority`** The signatory must hold delegated authority for contract_value under the delegation-of-authority matrix.
- **`ct.dpa_precedes_processing`** Where data_processing_in_scope is true, personal data must not flow before an executed DPA exists.
- **`ct.amendment_authority`** An amendment requires the same authority level as the instrument it varies.
- **`ct.survival_clauses_outlive_term`** Confidentiality, audit, data-deletion and indemnity obligations commonly survive expiry. _(soft)_
- **`ct.no_work_before_countersignature`** Work performed before countersignature is performed on terms nobody has agreed. _(soft)_


## Business rules

- **`ct.notice_deadline_is_the_real_deadline`** A renewal decision must be recorded on or before end_at minus notice_period_days. Any diary entry, brief or review scheduled against end_at instead is scheduled against the wrong date.
 — _This is the rule the object exists to enforce. Everything else here is support for it._
- **`ct.unknown_auto_renew_treated_as_true`** A null auto_renew is treated as true until the clause has been read and the read is recorded. — _Optimism about a field nobody has checked is how a register acquires contracts it cannot exit._
- **`ct.auto_renew_requires_named_owner`** An auto-renewing contract with no business_owner_ref cannot be recorded as complete. — _Nobody is on the hook for a decision that makes itself, so the decision does not get made._
- **`ct.no_executed_copy_no_active_state`** A contract cannot be recorded active while countersigned is false or signed_copy_held is false. — _An active state on an unexecuted instrument makes the register report coverage it does not have._
- **`ct.notice_must_use_the_contractual_method`** Service by a method other than notice_method, or to an address other than notice_recipient, does not count as served.
- **`ct.legal_review_before_countersignature`** Above the policy threshold, countersignature with no recorded legal review is a control failure regardless of how routine the paper looked. — _The routine-looking paper is where the unusual clause hides, because nobody negotiates the boring ones._
- **`ct.amendment_does_not_reset_notice`** An amendment does not restart the notice clock unless it expressly restates the term. — _Diarising the renewal from the amendment date is the most common single cause of a missed window._
- **`ct.evergreen_needs_a_diarised_review`** A contract with is_evergreen true and no scheduled review date will never be reviewed again. — _Nothing in the instrument will ever prompt anyone. The prompt has to be manufactured or it does not exist._
- **`ct.renewal_without_a_recorded_decision_is_a_miss`** Where renewal_decision_recorded_at is null on the day after notice_deadline_at, the renewal is logged as a default, not as a decision.
 — _Layer 6 learns nothing from renewals recorded as decisions. Counting defaults honestly is the only way the notice-window hit rate means anything, and it is the number that makes the case for the whole capability.
_
- **`ct.order_form_requires_its_framework`** An order form, call-off or SOW recorded without a parent MSA or framework is incomplete, not merely unlinked.


## Exceptions — where the rules above are legitimately wrong

- **An evergreen contract has no expiry, so notice_deadline_at cannot be computed and the renewal rule does not apply to it.** — The correct substitute is a diarised periodic review, set from criticality, plus a standing note of the notice period so the exit can be exercised at any time. Applying the expiry rule to an evergreen produces a null and then silence, which is how these contracts run for a decade — the control does not fail loudly, it simply never engages.
 _(overrides ct.notice_deadline_is_the_real_deadline)_
- **Where an amendment expressly restates the term or the notice period, it DOES reset the clock and the parent's dates are superseded.** — The general rule exists because most variations are silent on term. The exception matters because the ones that are not silent are usually the extensions, which are exactly the instruments whose dates people are trying to work out.
 _(overrides ct.amendment_does_not_reset_notice)_
- **A call-off under a framework inherits the framework's notice and termination provisions, not its own apparent term.** — The call-off's end date looks like the operative date and is not. Administering call-offs as standalone contracts produces a register with dozens of small correct-looking rows and one real exit date nobody has recorded.
 _(overrides ct.notice_deadline_is_the_real_deadline, ct.order_form_requires_its_framework)_
- **Where the counterparty accepts service by another method in writing, that acceptance is itself a variation and email notice is then valid.** — Refusing to accept a written waiver is over-application of a good rule. The discipline is that the waiver must be filed with the notice — an unfiled waiver is indistinguishable from an improperly served notice a year later, when the person who agreed it has left.
 _(overrides ct.notice_must_use_the_contractual_method, ct.service_method_binds)_
- **Work may begin before countersignature under a written letter of intent with a hard expiry and a named ratification date.** — A control that cannot bend under commercial pressure gets bypassed permanently rather than temporarily. The expiry on the LOI is what keeps the exception an exception; an LOI with no expiry quietly becomes the operative agreement, on terms drafted in an afternoon.
 _(overrides ct.no_work_before_countersignature, ct.no_executed_copy_no_active_state)_
- **For utilities, regulated services and most large-platform SaaS the terms are dictated, and legal review is a record rather than a control.** — Routing a standard cloud order form through a full review consumes the legal capacity that the one genuinely negotiable contract that quarter needed. The right response is to record the accepted position and its risk, not to pretend a negotiation happened.
 _(overrides ct.legal_review_before_countersignature)_
- **Expiry does not discharge confidentiality, audit, data-deletion or indemnity obligations, so an expired contract may still generate live obligations on us.** — Retention and obligation tracking must run from the end of the survival period, not from expiry. Archiving on the expiry date is how a data-deletion obligation is missed by a business that believed the relationship was over.
 _(overrides ct.notice_deadline_is_the_real_deadline)_
- **Intra-group agreements need term and transfer-pricing rigour but not counterparty diligence or exit planning.** — Applying the third-party model to a group entity produces theatre. Applying no model at all produces a transfer-pricing finding, which is the failure mode that actually occurs.
 _(overrides ct.auto_renew_requires_named_owner)_


## Best practices

- **Abstract the contract once, in the week of signature — obligations on us, notice period, notice method, uplift basis, liability cap.** — It is the only week in the life of the contract when somebody who understands it is available and motivated. Every later attempt is archaeology performed by somebody who was not there, usually under time pressure created by the very deadline they missed.

- **Schedule the renewal work backwards from notice_deadline_at, with a lead time scaled to value and switching cost.** — A fixed thirty-day reminder is right for nothing. A large outsourcing contract with a six-month notice period needs the brief starting nine months before expiry; a small software subscription needs a week. One lead time for both means the big one is always late and the small one is always noise.

- **Produce the renewal brief before the window opens, not inside it.** — A brief written inside the window is an argument for renewing, because by then there is no time to do anything else and everybody in the room knows it. The brief is only a decision document while the alternative is still achievable.

- **Where the renewal decision is genuinely undecided at the deadline, serve protective notice and carry on negotiating.** — It converts a deadline into an option at the price of one awkward conversation. Most counterparties expect it on large agreements; the ones who react badly are telling you something useful about the relationship. The alternative is renewing by default and calling it a decision.

- **Record a named business owner as a condition of the register entry being complete, at signature and not at renewal.** — The person who negotiated it is identifiable on the day it is signed and untraceable three years later. Naming the owner late means naming whoever currently holds the budget code, who has no idea what was agreed.

- **Hold and present the register ordered by notice_deadline_at, not alphabetically and not by value.** — Sort order is the cheapest control in contract administration. A register sorted by supplier name is a list; sorted by the next irreversible date it is a work queue, and the work it queues is the work that actually expires.

- **Check the signatory against the delegation-of-authority matrix at execution, automatically, on every instrument.** — It is a numeric comparison against a table the organisation already maintains, and it is almost universally done retrospectively by an auditor instead. Done at signature it is a question; done at audit it is a finding.

- **Execute the DPA in the same signature envelope as the commercial contract where data is in scope.** — Split into a separate workflow it goes to the back of a queue that has no deadline, while the data starts flowing on the commercial start date. Same envelope, same day, one chase instead of nine.

- **Count renewals that happened by silence separately from renewals that were decided, and report both by value.** — A function that reports "98% of contracts renewed successfully" is reporting that it did not act. The uncomfortable number is the one that funds the capability.



## Anti-patterns

- **A contract register that stores end dates and not notice deadlines.** — tempting because The expiry date is on the front page of the contract and the notice period is in clause 21. Whoever built the register captured what was easy to capture, and every row looks populated.
 Instead: Compute and store notice_deadline_at at entry, make it a required field, and sort the register by it.
- **The renewal is discovered when an invoice arrives showing a new contract period.** — tempting because Nobody owns the contract, the spend is already in the budget from last year, and the invoice is within tolerance so it passes the three-way match without a human reading it.
 Instead: Emit the notice-window event to a named owner with the silence cost attached, and require a recorded decision either way.
- **One fixed reminder lead time applied to every contract regardless of notice period, value or switching cost.** — tempting because It is a single configuration line, it is defensible in a policy document, and it means nobody has to think about individual contracts.
 Instead: Scale lead time from notice_period_days, contract_value and switching cost. Three tiers is enough.
- **Abstracting only what the counterparty owes us and none of what we owe them.** — tempting because The abstraction is usually done by whoever will manage the supplier's performance, and their job is what the supplier does. Nobody's job is what we do.
 Instead: Abstract both sides, and log the obligations on us as owned commitments with due dates.
- **Diarising the renewal from the date of the latest amendment rather than from the term the amendment governs.** — tempting because The amendment is the most recent document in the folder and it has a date on it. The reasoning is superficially sound and the error is invisible until the window has passed.
 Instead: Inherit the parent's dates unless the amendment expressly restates the term, and record which instrument each date came from.
- **Serving notice by email because that is how we always talk to them, where the clause requires registered post.** — tempting because Emailing the account manager we have dealt with for six years feels more real than posting a letter to a registered office nobody has ever visited. It also gets an immediate acknowledgement, which feels like proof.
 Instead: Serve by the contractual method to the contractual address with proof of delivery, and separately email the human as a courtesy.
- **Routing contracts to legal review with no service level and no visibility of dwell time.** — tempting because Legal is a scarce internal function and nobody wants to be the person who put an SLA on the general counsel. Cycle time is then reported as a supplier problem.
 Instead: Count dwell time from the legal_review observation. Publishing the number is usually sufficient; it is almost always smaller than legal fears and larger than the business assumes.
- **Recording the order form as the contract because it is the document with the price on it.** — tempting because The order form is what came back signed and what procurement needed for the purchase order. The MSA was agreed two years earlier by people who have left.
 Instead: Make the parent instrument a required link on any call-off, order form or SOW, and refuse to mark the entry complete without it.
- **The contract is signed by whoever was available and senior-looking rather than by the person the matrix names.** — tempting because The counterparty wants it back by Friday, the named signatory is on leave, and the alternative is a delay the business will blame on administration.
 Instead: Maintain a delegation matrix with named deputies, and automate the value check at execution rather than at audit.
- **Closing and archiving the contract on its expiry date, treating expiry as discharge.** — tempting because Expiry is the visible end of the relationship, the budget line closes, and the folder moves to the archive. Survival clauses are in the boilerplate nobody reads twice.
 Instead: Set retention from the end of the survival period, and keep surviving obligations on the live obligation register after the contract state moves to retained.

## Inputs

- **email** — paper requested, redlines exchanged, who moved last
- **email** — which side is holding the draft
- **derived** — abstracted obligations logged as commitments
- **contract** — term, notice period, auto-renewal, liability cap, service clauses
- **document** — executed counterpart, amendments, order forms, schedules
- **signed_form** — e-signature completion certificate with signer identity and timestamp
- **erp** — committed spend, payment terms, invoices matched to the instrument
- **register** — the contract register itself — dates, owners, renewal decisions
- **portal** — the counterparty's own contract portal
- **manual_entry** — notice deadline diarised by an administrator who actually read the clause


## Outputs

- **`notice_deadline_at`** The date a renewal decision must exist by. Everything else schedules backwards from this. → L4.reasoning_unit, L5.execution_planning
- **`days_to_notice_deadline`** Urgency as a number. Negative means the contract has already renewed and nobody has noticed. → L4.reasoning_unit, L4.decision_maker
- **`silence_cost`** What doing nothing costs. The only way a silent item competes for attention against noisy ones. → L4.decision_maker, L5.execution_planning
- **`obligation_register`** Duties on us with due dates, structured for scheduling rather than for reading. → L4.reasoning_unit, L5.execution_planning
- **`renewal_brief`** Spend, performance, alternatives and switching cost, assembled BEFORE the window opens. A brief produced inside the window is an argument for renewing. → L5.communication_planning
- **`notice_service_instruction`** Contractually valid method and addressee. The channel planner must not default to email where the clause says registered post. → L5.2.channel_planner
- **`contract_coverage_flag`** Whether spend with this counterparty is under paper at all. → L4.decision_maker
- **`enforceability_gap`** True where no executed counterpart can be produced. A contract we cannot produce is a contract we do not have. → L4.reasoning_unit, L6.learning_unit
- **`signature_authority_check`** Whether the signatory held delegated authority for this value. → L4.decision_maker, L6.learning_unit


## Events

- **`ct.paper_requested`** Contract Requested
- **`ct.legal_review_opened`** Legal Review Opened
- **`ct.executed`** Contract Executed
- **`ct.notice_window_opened`** Notice Window Opened
- **`ct.auto_renewed_by_default`** Auto-Renewed By Default — invalidates renewal_decision_recorded_at
- **`ct.notice_served`** Notice Served
- **`ct.obligation_breached`** Obligation On Us Breached
- **`ct.terms_varied`** Terms Varied By Amendment — invalidates notice_deadline_at, contract_value, obligations_on_us
- **`ct.counterparty_changed`** Counterparty Changed By Novation Or Acquisition — invalidates notice_recipient, counterparty_ref, signatory_them
- **`ct.expired`** Contract Expired


## Actions

- **Abstract the obligations on us** (human) — Read the contract once, at execution, and record what we owe and when. The cheapest hour in contract administration and the one nobody has.
- **Diarise the notice deadline** (system) — Create a deadline at end_at minus notice_period_days, with lead time scaled to value and switching cost rather than a fixed thirty days.
- **Route to legal review** (human) —
- **Chase the counterparty for the draft** (agent) —
- **Nudge the internal holder of the paper** (agent) — To a named person, not the function mailbox. Contract delay is overwhelmingly internal and almost never attributed internally.
- **Confirm countersignature and file the executed copy** (human) — Closes the enforceability gap in the week both sides still care. Nearly impossible to close in year four.
- **Assemble the renewal brief** (agent) — Spend, performance, alternatives, switching cost — before the window opens. A brief produced inside the window is an argument for renewing.
- **Serve notice of termination** (human) — By the contractual method, to the contractual address, with proof of delivery retained. Irreversible, which is why it stays a human action.
- **Serve protective notice to preserve optionality** (human) — Terminate to prevent auto-renewal while continuing to negotiate. Converts a deadline into an option, at the cost of a conversation the business will not enjoy.
- **Open renegotiation** (human) — Leverage exists only inside the notice window. Outside it we are asking rather than negotiating, and the counterparty knows the date as well as we do.
- **Verify the signatory held authority** (system) — Check signatory_us against the delegation-of-authority matrix for contract_value. Cheap, automatable, and almost never done.


## Evidence

- **contract** · 10000 bp — The executed instrument. Nothing outranks it and nothing substitutes for it in a dispute.
- **signed_form** · 9500 bp — E-signature completion certificate with audit trail. Proves who signed, when, and from where.
- **register** · 7500 bp — The contract register. Authoritative for dates only to the extent somebody read the clause — treat it as a claim ABOUT the contract, not as the contract.
- **erp** · 7000 bp — Committed spend and payment history. Proves the relationship is live even where the paper cannot be found, which is a surprisingly common configuration.
- **document** · 7000 bp — Amendments, order forms, schedules, the DPA. Each is a contract fragment and the operative terms are the union of them.
- **email** · 5500 bp — Agreement in correspondence. It can bind us — which is the risk, not the value. An email accepting revised terms is a variation whether or not anyone filed it.
- **portal** · 5000 bp — The counterparty's contract portal. Their record of our terms; convenient, and never wrong in our favour.
- **manual_entry** · 4000 bp — An administrator's abstraction. Only as good as the read, and it is never re-read after the person who made it leaves.
- **derived** · 3000 bp — Inferred from thread movement and spend behaviour. Corroborating only, never sole grounds for a statement about the terms.


## Metrics

- **notice_window_hit_rate** (percent) — Share of renewals decided before notice_deadline_at. The one number that says whether contract administration is running at all.
- **default_renewal_rate** (percent) — Share of renewals that happened because nobody acted. Report alongside its value, not as a count — three defaults can be worth more than thirty decisions.
- **renewal_decision_lead_time** (days) — Days between the recorded decision and the notice deadline. Negative values are not late decisions; they are non-decisions.
- **executed_copy_completeness** (percent) — Share of active contracts whose executed counterpart can be produced within one working day.
- **obligation_capture_rate** (percent) — Share of active contracts with obligations abstracted. Usually the lowest number in this list, and the cheapest to move.
- **contract_cycle_time** (days) — Request to countersignature. Splits cleanly into our delay and theirs once ball_in_court is tracked, and the split is usually the reverse of the story the business tells.
- **uncontracted_spend_share** (percent) — Spend with counterparties holding no active contract.
- **unapproved_uplift_value** (money) — Price increases absorbed without a recorded approval. The quietest line item in any budget.
- **legal_review_dwell_time** (days) — Days paper spends in legal review. Unmeasured in most organisations because the observation exists and nothing counts it.

## Examples

- **36-month SaaS subscription, 90 days' notice, auto_renew true** _(typical)_ — Expiry in March means the decision date is December, in the quarter nobody is looking and half the owners are on leave. The archetype this object was built for.
- **Evergreen cleaning contract signed in 2019, RPI-linked, uncapped** _(typical)_ — No end date, no owner, no benchmark. Never re-decided; the annual cost has risen by a third without a single approval, one invoice at a time.
- **Six-month notice on a facilities outsourcing agreement** _(edge)_ — The renewal brief has to start nine months before expiry. Any register on a fixed thirty-day reminder has already lost this one before the reminder fires.
- **Order form on file, MSA agreed in 2021 by people who have left** _(misclassification)_ — Recorded in the register as the contract. It is not: it is the price list. The liability cap and the notice period sit in a document nothing points at.
- **Amendment extending term by 12 months, silent on notice** _(edge)_ — Notice period unchanged from the parent. Diarising from the amendment date loses the window by the length of the original term.
- **Letter of intent, no expiry, work started, MSA never signed** _(edge)_ — Eighteen months of delivery on two pages drafted in an afternoon. The LOI is now the operative agreement and nobody decided that.
- **Terminated by email where the clause required registered post** _(counterexample)_ — Not served. The renewal ran, the invoice arrived, and the file said cancelled. Two records of the same contract, both confident, one wrong.
- **Invoice from a supplier with no contract in the register** _(misclassification)_ — Usually read as a missing register entry. It is more often maverick spend: the agreement is the purchase order and the terms are whatever was printed on the back of their invoice.
- **NDA signed at first contact three years ago, still in force** _(edge)_ — Perpetual confidentiality obligation, no commercial relationship, no owner, no review. Harmless until we hire from them or they are acquired by a competitor.
- **DPA required, never executed, personal data flowing since the start date** _(counterexample)_ — A finding at the next audit and a notification obligation if the processor is breached. The commercial contract was signed on time; the one that made the processing lawful was not.

## Metadata

owner **Admin** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional** · completeness **complete**


> Rewritten onto the 23-section schema. Six of sixteen patterns are executable and all six read the negotiation rather than the instrument: contract_requested, legal_review, thread.ball_in_court, thread.last_inbound, derived.engagement and commitment.due_at. The ten that cannot fire share one root cause — nothing in Layer 1 reads a contract register or a CLM, so end_at, notice_period_days and auto_renew, the three fields that decide every renewal in the business, are invisible to the pipeline.
Ranked backlog this object generates. (1) contract.end_at and contract.notice_period_days (L1) — without them notice_deadline_at cannot be computed and the object's central deliverable does not exist. (2) contract_countersigned (L2) — the cheapest line here; the pack already observes the request and drops the execution, which is the exact moment obligations attach to us. (3) notice_served (L2) — an absence can only be a trigger if the presence is observable. (4) contract.auto_renew (L1) — until it exists every contract must be treated as auto-renewing, which is correct and expensive.
The honest reading of this file is that the contract-administration capability cannot yet do its main job and can already do the second-order one: measuring where paper sits and who is holding it up. That is worth shipping while the register connector is built.
